utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'Costa Mesa' by name among the cities in its service area.

generation_supplier.notes: Orange County Power Authority (OCPA) representatives have proposed a feasibility study for potential Costa Mesa membership, per reporting on a City Council discussion, but Costa Mesa is not yet an OCPA member community. Left null rather than recording a program that is not yet operational for this city.

county.notes: Costa Mesa is a well-documented Orange County city; also listed under Orange County in SCE's own service-area fact sheet.

permit_authority.notes: costamesaca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session (including the bare domain root), and ecode360.com (host of the city's Small Residential Solar Energy System Permits municipal code chapter) also returned HTTP 403. This department name and page title are confirmed via search-engine indexing, but the page's specific content (eligibility, fees, timeline) could not be independently verified.

permit_url.notes: URL identified via search-engine indexing; costamesaca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, so its content could not be independently read or verified.

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes Costa Mesa/Orange County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

required_documents.notes: costamesaca.gov returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch on every attempt this session, blocking access to the city's solar submittal requirements page.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Search-engine summaries indicate Costa Mesa processes solar via its own TESSA online permitting system rather than SolarAPP+, but no size-cap or property-type figure could be independently confirmed via direct fetch this session.
